newsitem.title: USA: Auditors to charge DC finances still a mess - paper.
newsitem.headline: Auditors to charge DC finances still a mess - paper.

text.p: KPMG Peat Marwick will charge in a fiscal 1996 audit for the District of Columbia on Tuesday that the city is failing to collect tens of millions of dollars in taxes and its financial operations are in chaos, the Washington Post reported on Friday.

The accounting firm will give the city's 1996 financial report, also due out on February 4, a "qualified opinion," the Post said. That means that Peat Marwick has considerable questions about the city's financial figures, the Post said.
The 1996 financial report shows that the city had a budget deficit of $74 million in fiscal 1996, which gives the city an accumulated deficit of close to a half-billion dollars, the Post said.

The Post said the upcoming findings show that D.C. Chief Financial Officer Anthony Williams "has failed to correct" many major problems that were highlighted by Peat Marwick last year in the firm's fiscal 1995 audit of the financially struggling city.
Williams' independent post was created by Congress in 1995 legislation establishing a financial control board for the city.
Williams acknowledged that the city's fiscal operations continue to face severe problems, but added that D.C.'s financial woes have been mounting for decades, the Post said.
Williams added he will need at least two more years to clean up the mess, the Post said.
